sumInsured: Not specified (varies as per Policy Schedule)

great.name: PED Waiting Period
great.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a pre -existing Disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 12 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with insurer.
great.explanation: Pre-existing diseases and their direct complications are not covered for the first 12 months from the first policy start date. Coverage for PEDs starts after 1 year, which is faster than many plans that take 2–4 years.

great.name: Restore Benefit
great.quote: The Company agrees to automatically make the re-instatement of up to the base Sum Insured once in a policy year... (iii) Recharge amount can be utilized for same illness as well as different Illnesses.
great.explanation: The base Sum Insured can be automatically reinstated once in a policy year after it is used. The restored amount can be used for the same illness or a different illness, improving protection against multiple hospitalizations.

great.name: No Claim Bonus
great.quote: enhance the Sum Insured by 25% flat, on a cumulative basis... (vii) In the event of a Claim occurring during any Policy Year, the accrued No Claim Bonus will be reduced at same rate at which it is accrued at the commencement of next Policy Year;
great.explanation: Sum Insured increases by 25% for each claim-free year (cumulative), and if a claim happens the bonus reduces by the same step instead of dropping to zero. This helps you retain part of the accumulated bonus even after a claim.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident, provided the same are covered.
good.explanation: Illness-related claims are not covered for the first 30 days from policy start, while accidents are covered immediately. This is a standard market waiting period.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the listed Conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage...
good.explanation: Listed diseases/surgeries are not covered for the first 24 months of continuous coverage. This is a common restriction for certain conditions in retail health plans.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: Under Pre-hospitalization Medical Expenses, for a period of 60days immediately prior to the Insured Person's date of admission to the Hospital
good.explanation: Medical expenses are covered for up to 60 days before hospital admission. This helps pay for consultations, tests, and medicines leading up to hospitalization.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: Under Post-hospitalization Medical Expenses, for a period of 90 days immediately after the Insured Person's date of discharge from the Hospital
good.explanation: Medical expenses are covered for up to 90 days after discharge. This supports follow-up treatment and medicines during recovery.

good.name: Domiciliary Hospitalization
good.quote: The Company will indemnify the Insured Person... for the Medical Expenses incurred towards Domiciliary Hospitalization... subject to the conditions specified below: (i) The Domiciliary Hospitalization continues for a period exceeding 3 consecutive days.
good.explanation: Home treatment is covered as domiciliary hospitalization if it continues for more than 3 consecutive days and meets the policy conditions. This can help when hospital admission is not possible or advisable.

good.name: Modern Treatments
good.quote: The Company will indemnify the Insured Person... for treatment taken through following advance technology methods: ... Robotic surgeries ... Stereotactic radio surgeries ...
good.explanation: Advanced technology methods like robotic surgeries and stereotactic radio surgeries are covered as per policy terms. This improves access to newer treatment options without needing a separate add-on.

bad.name: Room Rent
bad.quote: If the Insured Person is admitted in a Hospital room where the Room Category opted or Room Rent incurred is higher than the eligible Room Category/ Room Rent as specified in|the Policy Schedule, then, a. The Policyholder/Insured Person shall bear the ratable proportion of the total Associate Medical Expenses...
bad.explanation: Eligible room category/room rent is limited as per the Policy Schedule, and choosing a higher room triggers ratable (proportionate) sharing of associated medical expenses. This can sharply increase out-of-pocket costs beyond just the room rent difference.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: Any item or condition or treatment specified in List of Non-Medical Items (Annexure - i to Policy Terms & Conditions).
bad.reference: Section 4.2 Specific Exclusions, point 1 + Annexure I (Non-medical items list includes e.g., "GLOVES", "MASK", etc.)
bad.explanation: Items listed as non-medical/consumables in Annexure I (e.g., gloves, masks) are excluded from payment. This can lead to meaningful out-of-pocket expenses during hospitalization.

bad.name: Co-pay (Optional)
bad.quote: If this Optional Benefit is opted... If the Insured Person takes Medical Treatment in hospitals other than those listed in Annexure – III... shall bear a Co Payment of 20% on each and every Claim... (ii) However, no such additional co-payment shall be applicable if treatment is availed in the hospitals listed in Annexure III
bad.explanation: If the Smart Select optional benefit is chosen, a 20% co-pay applies on each and every claim when treatment is taken outside the hospitals listed in Annexure III. This means you may have to pay 20% of admissible bills yourself, which is a major cost risk.

unclear.name: Disease Sub-limits
unclear.quote: If this Optional Benefit is opted, then there shall be sub-limits on listed treatments and procedures up to the amount specified against each treatment and procedures in the Policy Schedule and Company's liability shall be limited to such extent. Listed Treatments and Procedures are as follows: (i) Treatment of Cataract (ii) Treatment of Total Knee Replacement ...
unclear.reference: Section 3.2.6 Optional Benefit: Sub-Limit on Specified Diseases
unclear.explanation: If this optional benefit is opted, certain listed treatments (e.g., cataract, total knee replacement) will be capped to amounts shown in the Policy Schedule. Whether it impacts you depends on if you choose this option and what sub-limits are stated in your schedule.

unclear.name: Cashless Network
unclear.quote: Cashless Facility means a facility extended by the insurer... directly made to the network Provider...
unclear.explanation: Cashless treatment is available at network providers as per the insurer’s process. The policy wording does not state the number of network hospitals, so you need to check the insurer’s current hospital list for your city.

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
